findings.issue: External library functions run by DELEGATECALL to linked addresses; in this unlinked bytecode the 8 targets are link placeholders (all 0x11...), not real addresses. The six loops of the source (CCTPLib.transferUSDCToCCTP's while, CurveLib's four for loops, PSMLib.swapUSDCToUSDS's while) are in those libraries, not in this bytecode.

findings.issue: Inner call data built at a constant-relative base decodes into a readable Array(...) argument, but when it is built after an array allocation at a loaded mem[64] the outer call stays raw memory and the inner selector shows only as a decimal (430596695 = 0x19aa6257).
findings.rule: Print a constant written to mem[a len n], n < 32, as Bytes(n, 0x...); fold mem[64] after 'mem[64] = b + k' (the known P2 root cause) so the second doCall decodes like the first.

notes: No loop of the source is in this bytecode: all six belong to external libraries reached by DELEGATECALL (see the artifact finding). The 7 whiles are compiler code: 5 element-wise memory copies of ABI encodings/decodings of uint256[] (removeLiquidityCurve 1905/1918, requestWithdrawFromWstETH 2636/2692/2705: P7) and 2 checked exponentiation helpers of 10**decimals (1980, 2087). Reviewed line by line: requestWithdrawFromWstETH, depositToWeETH, the admin setters (setMaxSlippage, setOTCBuffer...); the other role-gated wrappers by structure (nonReentrant guard stor0, hasRole check reverting with AccessControlUnauthorizedAccount(caller, role), rate-limit call on stor40, proxy.doCall); all faithful. The rate-limit keys (LIMIT_*) are storage variables in this version, and the text reads them as storN correctly. Custom errors print as raw selectors (0x3ee5aeb5 ReentrancyGuardReentrantCall, 0xe2517d3f AccessControlUnauthorizedAccount).
summary: Faithful, mostly readable text of role-gated wrappers; it has no source loops of its own (they are in delegatecalled libraries with placeholder addresses), and its main blemishes are decimal selectors and a few undecoded nested proxy calls.
